1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project Overview
6	
7	Metaformalism Copilot is a Next.js web app for transforming insights and source material into personalized, context-sensitive formalisms. It's part of the [Live Conversational Threads](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/uueHkKrGmeEsKGHPR/live-conversational-threads-not-an-ai-notetaker-2) research project. The philosophy ("Live Theory") emphasizes generalization via inclusion — producing multiple rigorous representations tailored to specific contexts rather than a single unified theory.
8	
9	## Prerequisites
10	
11	- Node.js 20+ and npm
12	- An `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` environment variable for LLM features (the call layer prefers Anthropic, falls back to OpenRouter, and returns mock responses if neither is set)
13	
14	## Commands
15	
16	All commands run from the repo root:
17	
18	```bash
19	npm run dev        # Start dev server at localhost:3000
20	npm run build      # Production build
21	npm run lint       # ESLint (eslint-config-next with core-web-vitals + typescript)
22	npm test           # Run tests (Vitest)
23	npm run test:watch # Run tests in watch mode
24	npm run test:ui    # Run tests with Vitest UI
25	```
26	
27	## Architecture
28	
29	The app is a **multi-panel workspace** with a collapsible Icon Rail sidebar for navigation. The root `page.tsx` orchestrates all state and renders the active panel via a `PanelShell` layout. State is persisted to localStorage via `useWorkspacePersistence` and survives page refreshes.
30	
31	### Directory Layout (under `app/`)
32	
33	- `page.tsx` — Root orchestrator: manages panel navigation, all workspace state, and delegates to panel components
34	- `layout.tsx` — Sets up fonts (EB Garamond serif + Geist Mono) and metadata
35	- `globals.css` — CSS variables (`--ivory-cream`, `--ink-black`, `--paper-shadow`) and Tailwind v4 config via `@theme inline`
36	- `components/layout/` — `PanelShell` (Icon Rail + focus pane layout), `IconRail` (sidebar navigation)
37	- `components/panels/` — One component per panel: `InputPanel`, `SemiformalPanel`, `LeanPanel`, `GraphPanel`, `NodeDetailPanel`, `CausalGraphPanel`, `StatisticalModelPanel`, `PropertyTestsPanel`, `DialecticalMapPanel`, `CustomArtifactPanel`, `AnalyticsPanel`
38	- `components/features/` — Feature modules organized by domain:
39	  - `source-input/` — `TextInput`, `FileUpload` (.txt, .doc, .docx, .pdf)
40	  - `context-input/` — `ContextInput`, `RefinementButtons`, `RefinementPreview`
41	  - `output-editing/` — `EditableOutput`; `ai-bars/InlineEditPopup` (Cmd+K) and `ai-bars/WholeTextEditBar`
42	  - `workspace-session/` — `WorkspaceSessionBar` for session switching
43	  - `session-banner/` — `SessionBanner` for per-panel session context
44	  - `artifact-selector/` — Artifact type selection UI
45	  - `causal-graph/` — Graph visualization components
46	  - `lean-display/` — Lean code display with syntax highlighting
47	  - `evidence-search/` — `FindEvidenceButton`, `EvidenceResultsSection`, `EvidencePaperCard` for grounding artifacts in published research
48	- `components/ui/` — Shared UI components and icons
49	- `hooks/` — Custom hooks: `useWorkspacePersistence`, `useWorkspaceSessions`, `useFormalizationPipeline`, `useDecomposition`, `useAutoFormalizeQueue`, `useAnalytics`, etc.
50	- `lib/types/` — TypeScript type definitions for panels, sessions, artifacts, decomposition
51	- `lib/llm/` — LLM integration (Anthropic SDK, schemas, caching)
52	- `lib/formalization/` — Shared artifact generation logic
53	- `lib/utils/` — Utilities (PDF parsing, LaTeX parsing, export, text selection)
54	- `lib/stores/` — Zustand stores: `evidenceStore` (evidence search results, persisted to localStorage)
55	- `lib/corpus/` — DD-009 corpus filesystem layer (sub-task S1): `CorpusFS` interface + error kinds (`types.ts`), folder-layout path builders (`paths.ts` — **not** `layout.ts`, which is a reserved Next.js filename), `workspace.json` codec (`manifest.ts`), OPFS adapter (`opfsAdapter.ts`), default-off dev flag (`flag.ts`), and the store storage-seam selector (`storeAdapter.ts`). Behind a flag; localStorage is still the default persistence path.
56	- `api/` — Next.js API routes for formalization, editing, verification, decomposition, analytics, evidence search
57	
58	### Key Patterns
59	
60	- **Feature-based folder structure**: components grouped by feature domain, not by type
61	- **Import alias**: `@/*` maps to the project root (configured in `tsconfig.json`)
62	- **Client components**: Panel components use `"use client"` since they manage state
63	- **Multiple artifact types**: semiformal, lean, causal-graph, statistical-model, property-tests, dialectical-map — each with a dedicated panel and API route. Users can also create **custom artifact types** with user-authored system prompts, generated via a generic `/api/formalization/custom` route.
64	- **Decomposition workflow**: extract propositions from sources into a dependency graph, then formalize per-node
65	- **Session management**: workspace sessions (global) and formalization sessions (per-scope) for tracking artifact history
66	- **Corpus persistence (DD-009, in progress)**: a `CorpusFS` abstraction in `lib/corpus/` will eventually replace localStorage with an OPFS-cached, FSA-folder + git-remote corpus. Sub-task S1 (the `CorpusFS` interface + OPFS adapter) is wired behind `lib/corpus/flag.ts` (`isCorpusEnabled()`), **default-off and dev-only** — enabling it starts from an empty corpus (no migration until S4), so it must not be turned on for end users yet. Note for tests: **jsdom has no OPFS**, so the OPFS adapter's success path is verified via an in-memory fake + an out-of-CI Playwright smoke (`docs/spikes/corpus-opfs-smoke.md`), not the Vitest suite.
67	
68	### Design System
69	
70	- CSS variables in `globals.css` are the source of truth for theming
71	- Tailwind CSS v4 with `@tailwindcss/postcss`
72	- Primary font: EB Garamond (serif); Mono: Geist Mono
73	- Styling uses both Tailwind classes and `var(--css-variable)` references
74	
75	## Deployment
76	
77	The app is designed to be self-hosted single-tenant: each end user clicks the "Deploy with Vercel" button in the README and runs their own copy with their own LLM provider key. The deploy form lists both `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`; users provide at least one. There is no shared hosted instance and no demo mode. Implications:
78	
79	- The codebase assumes one trust boundary per deployment. There is no in-browser BYO-key flow; keys live in the Vercel project's environment variables (or `.env.local` in dev).
80	- The Lean verifier is a separate Dockerized service and cannot run inside a Vercel Function. When `LEAN_VERIFIER_URL` is unset or unreachable, `app/api/verification/lean/route.ts` falls back to a mock `{ valid: true, mock: true }` response. This is a known silent-pass behavior — `useFormalizationPipeline` treats it as `valid` and there is currently no "verifier offline" UI state. Anything depending on real type-checking must require the verifier explicitly.
81	- Persistence on Vercel is best-effort. The LLM cache (`app/lib/llm/cache.ts`) and analytics log (`app/lib/analytics/persist.ts`) write to a directory under `cwd()`, which is read-only on Vercel — those writes currently throw and are silently swallowed. Even after the writes are redirected to a writable path, only `/tmp` is writable on Vercel Functions and it lasts only as long as the warm container, so cache hits don't survive cold starts. Don't add features that assume durable filesystem state without an explicit storage backend.
82	
83	When changing user-facing setup steps, env vars, or deploy expectations, update both `README.md` (Deploy to Vercel section) and this file.
84	
85	## Code Guidelines
86	
87	- TypeScript for all components
88	- Tailwind CSS for styling; theme colors via CSS variables in `globals.css`
89	- Components should be modular and single-responsibility
90	- Follow existing feature-based folder structure in `app/components/features/`
91	- Ensure `npm run lint` passes before committing
92	
93	## Git Workflow
94	
95	- Always work on feature branches, never commit directly to main
96	- Commit after each logical unit of work with conventional commit messages (feat:, fix:, refactor:, test:, docs:)
97	- Push the branch after each commit so work is backed up remotely
98	- Before finishing a session, ensure all work is committed and pushed
99	- When asked to prepare for review, do an interactive rebase to clean up WIP commits into logical chunks
100	
101	## Code Quality
102	
103	- Tests use Vitest with React Testing Library. Write tests alongside implementation.
104	- Add comments explaining "why" for non-obvious library usage or architectural choices
105	- When choosing a new library or significant architectural approach, create a short decision record in `docs/decisions/NNN-title.md` explaining what was chosen and why
106	
107	## Documentation Maintenance
108	
109	When making changes that affect user-facing behavior, project structure, or available commands, check whether the following docs need updating:
110	
111	- `README.md` — UI description, available scripts, prerequisites, project documentation links
112	- `CLAUDE.md` — Architecture section, directory layout, commands, key patterns
113	- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — Component hierarchy and technical details
114	- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — Project structure section, code guidelines
115	
116	If a PR adds a new panel, artifact type, API route, script, or dependency, update the relevant docs in the same PR.
117	
118	## PR Preparation
119	
120	- Generate detailed PR descriptions including: summary of changes, motivation/context, how to test, and areas of uncertainty or risk
121	- Flag sections where you used unfamiliar libraries or patterns that the reviewer should scrutinize
122	- Note which tests (if any) cover which functionality
123	- Keep PRs to one reviewable concept; prefer multiple smaller PRs over one large one

content.content:
- **User-picked FSA folder** is the user-visible source of truth on disk. On first run (or workspace create), the app prompts for a folder; the folder *is* the corpus.
- **User-configured git remote** is the cross-device sync surface. Push/pull on commit; offline-capable through the OPFS cache and the local git working tree inside the folder.
- **Read path**: OPFS first (fast); fall through to FSA folder if OPFS is empty (recovery after browser-storage clear).
- **Write path**: writes commit to OPFS synchronously (no UI wait); async mirror to FSA folder (with retry); async push to remote (with backoff).
- **Degraded modes**: no FSA permission → OPFS-only (full read/write; user can connect a folder later and trigger one-time mirror). No git remote → local-only (folder works, manual cross-device via user's existing filesystem cloud-sync if they want it).

Folder layout (concrete proposal — to be refined in the implementation plan):

```
<corpus-root>/
├── workspaces/
│   └── <workspace-slug>/
│       ├── workspace.json               # manifest: sources, panels, current versions
│       ├── sources/
│       │   └── <source-id>.{txt,pdf,...}
│       ├── artifacts/
│       │   ├── semiformal/
│       │   │   ├── v0001.md
│       │   │   ├── v0002.md             # full history; `git diff` / `git blame` work
│       │   │   └── meta.json            # provenance per version
│       │   ├── causal-graph/...
│       │   └── custom/
│       │       └── <custom-type-id>/...
│       ├── custom-types/
│       │   └── <custom-type-id>.json    # the DEFINITION (also versioned via git)
│       └── decomposition/
│           ├── nodes/
│           │   └── <node-id>/artifacts/...
│           └── graph-layout.json
└── settings.json                        # workspace-list metadata
```

**Falsifiable hypothesis** (window: 6 weeks post-deploy of v1):
*A researcher who has used the app on device A picks up the workspace on device B by cloning their remote and opening the app in <5 minutes, with no version-history loss and all custom type definitions intact. Counter-evidence would be (a) session-switch tests still drop any artifact version, (b) cross-device cold-start exceeds 10 minutes, or (c) >20% of users in the first month report inability to complete FSA + git remote setup without out-of-band help.*

**Rationale for choosing #4' over its closest rivals:**

- **vs #4** (FSA + isomorphic-git, no OPFS cache): identical corpus property, but #4 leaves Firefox/Safari users with no working mode (FSA gaps). #4' degrades gracefully to OPFS-only there, preserving F10 partially (corpus exists, just not yet user-visible until the user switches browsers or downloads an export).
- **vs #5** (OPFS + git push only): identical browser breadth, but #5 leaves the user-visible folder optional/absent. #4''s opt-in FSA mirror gives F10 its strongest reading (corpus literally visible in Finder/Explorer) without sacrificing browser breadth — pay the full price only if the user wants it.
- **vs #9** (per-version sidecars, no git): #9 loses git's `log`/`diff`/`blame` primitives that directly serve F6 (no-loss provenance) and external readability. Without git, every consumer of the corpus has to learn our custom version scheme — directly contradicts F10's externalization goal. Boring-alternative move applied and rejected in stress-test.

=====FAILDRIVEN
94:- **Failure-driven mitigation** — enumerating new failure modes added a hard requirement to the chosen approach: every failure mode must surface in the UI rather than silently degrading. The implementation plan must include a "corpus status" UI element with at least four explicit states: FSA-permission-revoked, OPFS-quota-warning, remote-auth-expired, browser-storage-cleared (FSA-mirror still intact). Silent fallback is disallowed.
95-
96-## Consequences
97-
98-**This makes easier:**
99-
100-- Session switching becomes a data-level operation: switching loads a different workspace folder (or git ref). No in-memory snapshot bridge to keep in sync — *custom-type bleed-across-sessions becomes structurally impossible* because there is no longer a "global custom-type slot in Zustand that survives setState."
101-- Version history is a property of the corpus (per-version files), not in-memory state — session switch can never flatten it.
102-- External tooling (`git log artifacts/semiformal/v0007.md`, `grep -r`, `vim`, custom scripts) works on a researcher's corpus without the app running.
103-- Adding a new artifact type means adding a folder convention, not adding a snapshot/restore field. The class of bug that produced this DD goes away.
104-- Custom artifact type definitions are versioned alongside their outputs; rolling back a definition rolls back its associated runs through the same git mechanism.
105-- Each Vercel deployment is single-tenant by design; the trust model is now explicit (browser → FSA folder → git remote — three named, user-chosen surfaces).
106-- Reproducibility: every artifact can be cited by `(repo-url, commit-sha, path)` triple — F8 (research-corpus citability) is satisfied as a side-effect even though it wasn't the primary framing.
--
111:- Browser-storage clears now lose work that hasn't been mirrored to the folder or pushed to the remote. Must surface mirror/push status in UI (see failure-driven mitigation above).
112-- Concurrent edits on two devices can produce git merge conflicts the user must resolve. v1 will use a conservative simplifying rule (per-artifact-file last-write-wins with a warning) and defer richer conflict UI to a follow-up.
113-- `isomorphic-git` in the browser has performance characteristics that need empirical validation on workspaces with 50–100MB of source PDFs. A spike on this should precede the full implementation.
114:- Two-stage write path (OPFS → FSA → remote) doubles the failure-mode surface; needs explicit status indicators and retry. (Mitigated by failure-driven move; cost remains.)
115-- Migration from existing localStorage state is a one-shot conversion; design must include a safe migration path that backs up the old data before deleting it.
116-- Single-maintainer maintenance cost of `isomorphic-git` as a dependency — bounded by the library's stability and active maintainership (current as of 2026), but a real ongoing tax.
117-- v1 still allows third-party services on the remote axis (GitHub/GitLab/self-hosted git) — privacy is only "by default" if the user picks a self-hosted remote or stays local-only. S7 (privacy by default) is satisfied for OPFS-only mode; for full mode the user makes the trust trade explicitly.
118-
119-## Revisit triggers
120-
121-*How to read: each entry is a concrete, observable condition that should prompt re-evaluating this decision. Future readers can grep this section when their context changes to see whether earlier decisions still apply.*
122-
123-- if `isomorphic-git` stalls or is abandoned upstream — last release >18 months, or critical CVE without patch within 60 days.
124-- if Vercel deployment model changes to allow durable server filesystem — would unlock cloud-backed option #7 as a contender.
125-- if browser FSA support consolidates (Firefox and Safari both ship the API stably) — the OPFS-cache layer's value proposition weakens because FSA alone covers browser breadth.
126-- if measured cross-device cold-start exceeds 60s p95 in production telemetry.

## Project state
- **Branch purpose**: deliver DD-009's foundational corpus filesystem layer — a `CorpusFS` interface + OPFS adapter behind a default-off flag — without changing the localStorage production path.
- **Position in larger initiative**: first of six sub-tasks (S0–S5) from the DD-009 decomposition; blocks S2 (FSA mirror), S3 (git pipeline), S4 (migration+session rewrite). DD-009 decision + both iso-git spikes are merged into this branch.
- **Blocked on**: user approval of `plan-corpus-s1.md` (RPI step 4 gate) before any implementation.

## Key findings (curated from research)
- **The bug DD-009 targets is real and located**: workspace-session switching uses a *lossy* bridge in `app/page.tsx:124-173` (`getWorkspaceSnapshot`/`resetWorkspaceToSnapshot`) that omits `customArtifactTypes`/`customArtifactData` and flattens `ArtifactRecord.versions[]` to current-version-only. The store's *own* `getSnapshot` (workspaceStore.ts:503-521) was later fixed to include them, but sessions don't use it. **S1 does not fix this — S4 does** (replace the bridge). [observed]
- **Five fragmented localStorage stores** exist: `workspace-zustand-v1` (main), `workspace-sessions-v1`, `metaformalism-sessions`, `evidence-store-v1`, legacy `workspace-v2`. S1 touches only the main store's storage path. [observed]
- **Invariants S1 must honor**: SSR safety (no OPFS during render — guard like `skipHydration`); transient-state sanitization on persist; Vercel client-only persistence. [observed]
- **jsdom has no OPFS** — the adapter's real I/O is untestable in Vitest; CI uses an in-memory `CorpusFS` fake + a shared contract test, real OPFS via out-of-CI Playwright (mirrors the spike harness). [observed]
- **Perf is de-risked** by both spikes (proceed-to-RPI); not an S1 concern beyond honoring lazy-`git.log` later (S3). Safari/OPFS remain pre-launch verification items. [observed]
- **iso-git `buffer` polyfill is NOT an S1 concern** — nothing imports iso-git until S3. [observed]

## Plan (summary — full steps in plan-corpus-s1.md)
1. `corpus/types.ts` — `CorpusFS` interface; single substrate-neutral `CorpusErrorKind` source feeding `CorpusError`+`CorpusWorkerError`; document `CorpusGit` as a separate interface over `CorpusFS`.
2. `corpus/paths.ts` — DD-009 folder-layout path builders + slug-traversal sanitization (named `paths.ts`, not `layout.ts`, which Next.js reserves under `app/`).
3. `corpus/manifest.ts` — `workspace.json` schema + fail-loud serialize/parse.
4. **(test-first)** `__tests__/workspaceStore-characterization.test.ts` — lock current localStorage round-trip as equivalence target.
5. **(test-first)** `corpus/__tests__/` — in-memory fake + shared contract test (incl. S4 many-small-files access pattern) + layout/manifest unit tests.
6. `corpus/opfsAdapter.ts` — OPFS impl with SSR guard + typed-error mapping (quota not swallowed).
7. `corpus/flag.ts` + minimal `workspaceStore.ts` wiring — **DI seam typed as the `CorpusFS` interface** (default-off, dev-only).
8. Adapter error-path tests + flag-routing tests.
9. Out-of-CI Playwright OPFS smoke (Chrome+FF).
10. Docs (CLAUDE.md + `docs/thoughts/corpus-fs-seam.md`).

Implementation order: `[1,2,3,4] → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8 → 10`; 9 any time after 6.

- No OPFS/`navigator.storage` access during SSR/render (guard + lazy init).
- Flag OFF must be byte-for-byte the current localStorage behavior (characterization test is the proof).
- Quota/failure paths reify into typed errors, never `console.warn`-swallowed (unlike workspaceStore.ts:44-46).

- `app/lib/corpus/__tests__/layout.test.ts` — path/slug tests (step 5, new test)

Confirmed all four leads by reading the files, plus one more. Findings:

**1. /repo/app/lib/corpus/types.ts:61-75 — worker-transport twin shipped with zero callers**
`CorpusWorkerError`, `toWorkerError`, `isCorpusWorkerError` are referenced only by their own definitions (grep across `app/` finds no importers, not even tests). They serialize an error across a worker boundary that S3 hasn't built yet.
Simpler form: delete all three; `{ __corpusError: true, detail, message }` is a three-line object literal to write when the worker actually exists.
failure_scenario: S3 lands with a different worker protocol (e.g. structured-clone of `CorpusError` directly, or a `{ok,err}` envelope) and a reviewer must decide whether the untested year-old helper is authoritative or vestigial; meanwhile every `CorpusErrorKind` edit forces a mechanical re-read of code nothing calls.

**2. /repo/app/lib/corpus/types.ts:42-49 — five of eight error kinds are never constructed**
`fsa-permission-revoked`, `remote-auth-expired`, `browser-storage-cleared`, `git-conflict` belong to S2/S3, and `not-found` is unconstructible *by design* — the interface contract two lines above (types.ts:17-18) says missing paths return `null`/`[]` and only "everything else rejects". Only `unavailable`, `io`, `quota-exceeded` are ever thrown (opfsAdapter.ts:52, 60, 81-82; manifest.ts:66).
Simpler form: ship the three kinds S1 throws; add kinds in the sub-task that throws them. Drop `not-found` outright since it contradicts the null-return contract.
failure_scenario: `describeCorpusError`'s switch and every future exhaustive consumer switch carry five unreachable branches that can't be covered by a test, so coverage gaps look intentional and dead-code detection is permanently muted for this union; a future author also reasonably writes `throw new CorpusError({kind:"not-found"})` from `readFile`, silently breaking the null-means-missing contract the fake and the adapter both rely on.

**3. /repo/app/lib/corpus/manifest.ts:86-114 — validation silently defaults in four places despite a FAIL-LOUD doc contract**
The header (manifest.ts:10-13) says a malformed manifest "must surface as a typed `CorpusError` ... never a silent default". The body then does the opposite four times: `label` falls back to `s.id` (line 89), `createdAt`/`updatedAt` fall back to `new Date().toISOString()` (lines 109-110), and `.filter(isObject)` (lines 87, 94) drops non-object entries from `sources`/`artifacts` before validation ever sees them, and `.filter((x): x is string ...)` (line 103) drops non-string `customTypeIds`.
Simpler form: pick one rule. Either `fail()` on each (consistent with the doc and with lines 83-84/88/95), or make `label`/`createdAt`/`updatedAt` optional in `WorkspaceManifest` so the fallback is the type's stated default rather than a hidden repair.
failure_scenario: a truncated write producing `{"sources":[{"id":"a"},"garbage",{...}]}` parses "successfully" with the garbage entry vanished and fresh timestamps stamped on — exactly the "masquerades as valid, masks data loss" outcome the file's own docstring forbids, and it surfaces later as an unexplained missing source with no error to trace.

**4. /repo/app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:87-105 vs 156-174 — `readFile` and `stat` are the same 12 lines, differing only in the last statement**
Both do getRoot → splitPath → walkDir → `if (!dir) return null` → try/getFileHandle/`isNotFound`→null → `getFile()`; then one returns bytes, the other `{ size }`. `rm` (139-154) is a third copy of the same skeleton with `removeEntry`.
Simpler form: one `async function openFile(path): Promise<{size:number; arrayBuffer():Promise<ArrayBuffer>} | null>` used by both; `readFile` becomes two lines, `stat` one. (This also removes the `dir!` non-null assertion at line 112, which is only safe because `walkDir` never returns null when `create` is true — a fact currently enforced by nothing.)
failure_scenario: any fix to the missing-path detection — e.g. adding a third `DOMException` name to `isNotFound`, or handling a browser that throws `TypeMismatchError` from `getFile()` instead of `getFileHandle()` — has to be applied in three places, and fixing two of three yields `readFile` returning null while `stat` throws for the same path, breaking the contract suite's paired `readFile`/`stat` assertion (corpusFsContract.ts) in a way that reads as a test bug.

**5. /repo/app/lib/corpus/paths.ts (all 110 lines) and manifest.ts:44-115 — two modules whose only non-test callers do not exist**
`storeAdapter.ts:55` builds its one path inline (`state/${name}.json`) and never imports `paths`; nothing imports `manifest`. storeAdapter.ts:11-12 admits it: "built but not used by the store until S4". The eleven builders and the codec are exercised solely by paths.test.ts / manifest.test.ts.
Simpler form: land S1 with `flag.ts`, `types.ts`, `opfsAdapter.ts`, `storeAdapter.ts`; bring `paths.ts`/`manifest.ts` in with S4, where the real call sites will pin down the actual signatures.
failure_scenario: S4 discovers the layout needs, say, a per-source content hash in the filename or a `manifestVersion` migration path, so the builders and their 119 lines of tests get rewritten anyway — but until then every refactor, dependency bump, and lint sweep pays maintenance on API surface whose shape was guessed rather than driven by a caller.

**6. /repo/app/lib/corpus/paths.ts:36-58, 70-72 — `workspaceSlug` and `safeSegment` are the same pipeline copy-pasted, and `workspaceDir` re-sanitizes an already-sanitized value**
The two functions differ only in a trailing `.toLowerCase()` and the error message; `normalize→SAFE_SEGMENT→collapse→trim→throw-if-empty` is duplicated verbatim. Separately, `workspaceDir(slug: string)` calls `workspaceSlug(slug)` on a parameter already named `slug`, so callers like `workspaceManifestPath`/`sourcePath` sanitize twice — and the test at paths.test.ts:44 passes `"my-slug"` (already a slug) while `workspaceSlug` is documented as taking a *title*.
Simpler form: one `function sanitizeSegment(v: string, opts?: {lower?: boolean})`, with `workspaceSlug`/`safeSegment` as one-line wrappers; and make `workspaceDir` take a slug and assert it, or take a title and name the parameter `title`.
failure_scenario: the traversal guard — described at paths.ts:17-19 as "the single choke point" — actually exists in two copies, so a hardening fix (e.g. rejecting `.` and `..` explicitly, or handling a new unicode normalization case) applied to `workspaceSlug` alone leaves `safeSegment` exploitable for source ids and custom-type ids, and the title/slug ambiguity means nobody can tell from a call site whether the value was already sanitized.

/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:1:# 009: Artifact corpus architecture — OPFS-cached, FSA-folder-and-git-remote source of truth
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:20:> The product treats the user's body of generated work — every artifact, every version, every custom artifact type definition — as a first-class **corpus** that exists outside this tool's data model: portable across devices the same user owns (F4) and preserving every version with attribution (F6), so the LLM tool becomes one of many that read from and write to that corpus, swappable without losing work. We selected this over F1 (sovereignty) and F3 (interop) because F10 subsumes their motivational content (both are *reasons* the corpus should be outside the tool) without pre-committing to a single storage mechanism, while F1 alone leaves cross-device unsolved and F3 alone exposes the broadest security surface. Diamond 2 generated solutions evaluated against F10+F4+F6 jointly; approaches that solve only F7 (internal cleanup) or F9 (snapshot-bridge patch) are out-of-scope, not alternatives.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:30:**Chosen approach: #4' — OPFS as the transparent local cache; user-picked FSA folder + user-configured git remote as the corpus (source of truth).**
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:35:- **User-picked FSA folder** is the user-visible source of truth on disk. On first run (or workspace create), the app prompts for a folder; the folder *is* the corpus.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:44:<corpus-root>/
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:72:- **vs #4** (FSA + isomorphic-git, no OPFS cache): identical corpus property, but #4 leaves Firefox/Safari users with no working mode (FSA gaps). #4' degrades gracefully to OPFS-only there, preserving F10 partially (corpus exists, just not yet user-visible until the user switches browsers or downloads an export).
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:73:- **vs #5** (OPFS + git push only): identical browser breadth, but #5 leaves the user-visible folder optional/absent. #4''s opt-in FSA mirror gives F10 its strongest reading (corpus literally visible in Finder/Explorer) without sacrificing browser breadth — pay the full price only if the user wants it.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:74:- **vs #9** (per-version sidecars, no git): #9 loses git's `log`/`diff`/`blame` primitives that directly serve F6 (no-loss provenance) and external readability. Without git, every consumer of the corpus has to learn our custom version scheme — directly contradicts F10's externalization goal. Boring-alternative move applied and rejected in stress-test.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:82:`[1]: ✗ on H2 — manual-zip cross-device burden too high to meet the portability requirement.` `[6]: invert-thesis eliminated — offline-broken plus auth-expiry-mid-edit cost defended the local cache.` `[7]: ✗ on H1 — corpus inside opaque DB rows is not parseable files outside the tool.` `[8]: ✗ on H1 — binary CRDT documents are not parseable by external tools in the F10 sense.` `[10]: H6 weakness — user runs own WebDAV server is operator burden compounded by S1 setup friction.` `[11]: discarded by Diamond 1 chosen framing — null option contradicts architectural-shift goal.` `[12]: organizational-survival risk on single-maintainer project — three sync targets = three failure modes plus three test surfaces.` `[13]: ⚠ on H5 — Electron/Tauri abandons web-only Vercel deployment model.` `[4]: superseded by #4' which adds OPFS cache for browser-breadth without losing #4's corpus property.` `[5]: superseded by #4' which adds the user-visible FSA folder option without losing #5's browser-breadth.` `[9]: boring-alternative considered in stress-test; rejected because loss of git's log/diff/blame primitives forces every consumer of the corpus to learn a custom version scheme — directly contradicts F10's externalization goal.` `Prior pruning grep: no matches found for "persist", "storage", "session", "artifact", "filesystem", "localStorage".`
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:94:- **Failure-driven mitigation** — enumerating new failure modes added a hard requirement to the chosen approach: every failure mode must surface in the UI rather than silently degrading. The implementation plan must include a "corpus status" UI element with at least four explicit states: FSA-permission-revoked, OPFS-quota-warning, remote-auth-expired, browser-storage-cleared (FSA-mirror still intact). Silent fallback is disallowed.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:101:- Version history is a property of the corpus (per-version files), not in-memory state — session switch can never flatten it.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:102:- External tooling (`git log artifacts/semiformal/v0007.md`, `grep -r`, `vim`, custom scripts) works on a researcher's corpus without the app running.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:106:- Reproducibility: every artifact can be cited by `(repo-url, commit-sha, path)` triple — F8 (research-corpus citability) is satisfied as a side-effect even though it wasn't the primary framing.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:110:- Initial setup adds steps (pick a folder, optionally configure a git remote) — soft constraint S1 (zero-config) is partially sacrificed for the corpus property. Mitigated by making OPFS-only the zero-config default; FSA and git are opt-in.
/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:128:- if OPFS-only fallback mode is the only mode used by >80% of users after first 3 months — the FSA-corpus property is YAGNI and the design should collapse to #5.

**Why feature-based structure?**
- Clear separation of concerns
- Easy to find related code
- Scales well as features grow

**Why CSS variables?**
- Single source of truth for theme
- Easy color scheme updates
- No component changes needed

**Why modular components?**
- Testable in isolation
- Reusable (e.g., icons, editing bars)
- Clear prop interfaces

**Why textarea over contentEditable?**
- Simpler state management
- Easier selection handling
- Future migration to editor library (e.g., writing.js) is planned

Findings below. All confirmed by reading both the new code and the existing helper.

---

**1. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:25` — `createDebouncedLocalStorage()` is a byte-for-byte re-implementation of `createDebouncedStorage()` in `/repo/app/lib/stores/evidenceStore.ts:20`**

Same 300ms trailing debounce, same `pending` timer, same try/catch-and-`console.warn` on `setItem`, same `removeItem` cancel-then-delete. The only difference is the warn string ("Failed to persist workspace..." vs "Failed to persist evidence store:"). The diff *moved* the workspaceStore copy into corpus/ rather than extracting it, so the codebase still has two copies at rest.

failure_scenario: The new module's own docs treat swallowed quota errors as a defect (`/repo/app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:14` explicitly calls out "it is NOT swallowed with console.warn the way the legacy localStorage adapter does"). When S4 reifies localStorage quota failures, or when the 300ms constant is tuned, the fix lands only in `storeAdapter.ts` and `evidenceStore.ts` keeps silently dropping evidence writes on a full quota. Extract one `createDebouncedLocalStorage(opts: { onError })` into `app/lib/utils/` (next to the existing `throttle.ts`) and have `evidenceStore.ts:48` consume it instead of its local copy.

---

**2. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/paths.ts:36` — `workspaceSlug()` re-implements `sanitizeFilename()` from `/repo/app/lib/utils/export.ts:35`**

Both take a user-authored title and produce a lowercase hyphenated filesystem-safe name; there is also a third private `slugify()` at `/repo/app/lib/utils/latexParser.ts:121`. `sanitizeFilename` is already the codebase's exported filename-safety helper and is used for on-disk folder names at `/repo/app/lib/utils/exportAll.ts:76` (`${idx}-${sanitizeFilename(node.label)}`).

failure_scenario: `sanitizeFilename` caps output at 60 chars (`.slice(0, 60)`); `workspaceSlug` has no length bound. A workspace titled with a long paper abstract produces a path segment over the ~255-byte OPFS/FSA name limit, so `getDirectoryHandle` throws and `wrap()` reports it as an opaque `{kind:"io"}` rather than a nameable error — and the same title yields a *different* folder name in the zip export than in the corpus, so exported and on-disk workspaces no longer correlate. Reuse `sanitizeFilename` (adding the throw-on-empty behavior as an option) rather than minting a second rule set.

---

**3. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/manifest.ts:60` — `isObject()` is a third verbatim copy**

Identical to `/repo/app/lib/stores/workspaceStore.ts:32` and `/repo/app/lib/utils/workspacePersistence.ts:116`, character for character (`typeof v === "object" && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v)`).

failure_scenario: Three private copies of the same type guard with no exported home means the next validator writes a fourth. Export one from `app/lib/utils/` (or `app/lib/types/`) and import it in all three; the diff already touches `workspaceStore.ts`, so this is the cheapest moment to consolidate.

---

**4. `/repo/app/lib/stores/__tests__/workspaceStore-corpus-flag.test.ts:63` — `fakeRoot` OPFS stub duplicated from `/repo/app/lib/corpus/__tests__/opfsAdapter.test.ts:52`**

Both define the same self-referential handle shape (`getFileHandle` returning `{getFile, createWritable}`, `getDirectoryHandle` returning `fakeRoot`, `removeEntry`, `async *keys(){}`), differing only in whether `createWritable` throws `QuotaExceededError`. Both files also duplicate the `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(navigator, "storage")` save/restore dance (`opfsAdapter.test.ts:14-23`, `workspaceStore-corpus-flag.test.ts:17-22`).

failure_scenario: The module already establishes the shared-fake convention with `/repo/app/lib/corpus/__tests__/inMemoryCorpusFs.ts`, but no equivalent exists for the OPFS handle layer. When `opfsAdapter.ts` starts calling a new handle method (e.g. `createSyncAccessHandle` for the S3 worker), only one of the two stubs gets it and the flag-routing test fails with an unrelated `TypeError`. Add a `createFakeOpfsRoot(opts)` alongside `inMemoryCorpusFs.ts` and have both tests import it.

---

**5. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:128` — path normalization triplicated inside the new module**

`readdir` inlines `path.replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, "").split("/").filter(Boolean)`, which is exactly the first line of `splitPath()` at `/repo/app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:58`; `/repo/app/lib/corpus/__tests__/inMemoryCorpusFs.ts:13` has the same regex a third time as `normalize()`.

failure_scenario: `paths.ts` is documented as "the only source of corpus paths" and the sole traversal choke point, yet it exports no normalize/split — so the guard lives in three unexported places. A hardening fix that rejects `..` segments applied to `splitPath` leaves `readdir` accepting `"a/../../secret"` and leaves the in-memory fake keyed differently from the real adapter, silently breaking the shared contract suite's substitutability claim. Export a single `normalizeCorpusPath`/`splitCorpusPath` from `paths.ts` and use it in all three call sites.

---

**6. (lower confidence) `/repo/app/lib/corpus/manifest.ts:57` and `:78` — per-call `new TextEncoder()` / `new TextDecoder()` against the established hoisted-encoder convention**

`serializeManifest` and `parseManifest` each allocate a fresh codec per invocation, whereas `/repo/app/lib/llm/streamLlm.ts:18` hoists a module-level `const encoder = new TextEncoder()`, and the diff's own `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:53-54` hoists `enc`/`dec` per adapter.

failure_scenario: Minor, but manifest serialize runs once per artifact write in S4; the inconsistency also means a future swap to a shared codec module has to touch two styles. Hoist to module scope to match `storeAdapter.ts`.

---

No existing feature-flag utility exists in the repo (grep for `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `featureFlag`, `isEnabled` returns nothing in `app/`), so `/repo/app/lib/corpus/flag.ts` is not a duplication. Likewise no existing browser-side path-join helper — `/repo/app/lib/utils/dataDir.ts` is Node-only (`import { join } from "path"`) and not reusable here. `CorpusError` is only the second `extends Error` class in the repo (alongside `OpenRouterError` at `/repo/app/lib/llm/callLlm.ts:18`) and the two share no structure, so it is not a duplicate.

content.text: All 8 finder angles are running in the background. While waiting, I've independently confirmed two facts: the corpus tests pass (69/69), and webpack's DefinePlugin does inline the optional-chained env read in flag.ts. I'll consolidate candidates and run verification once the finders report.

Findings below. Confirmed the hot path: `page.tsx:814` wires the source textarea's `onChange` straight to `setSourceText` (`workspaceStore.ts:321`), and zustand's persist wraps every `set()` with `setItem()` (`/repo/node_modules/zustand/middleware.js:360-378`) — so one storage write per keystroke, unconditionally.

**1. Corpus `setItem` has no debounce; the localStorage path it replaces has 300ms**
- File: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63` (vs `:29-39`)
- Summary: the flag-ON storage seam writes synchronously-per-`set()` while the flag-OFF seam coalesces to one write per 300ms idle.
- failure_scenario: typing 40 chars into the source textarea (~5s) fires ~40 `setItem`s. Each does `JSON.stringify` of the full partialized workspace (sourceText + all artifact version arrays + customArtifactData — 100s of KB to MBs), a `TextEncoder.encode` full-byte copy, `navigator.storage.getDirectory()`, `getDirectoryHandle("state")`, `getFileHandle`, `createWritable`, `write`, `close`. The OFF path does ~2 localStorage writes for the same input. Cheaper: wrap `createCorpusBackedStorage` in the same debounce (or hoist the debounce above the seam so both adapters inherit it), keeping only the latest value.

**2. No write serialization — concurrent OPFS writes can commit out of order**
- File: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63`
- Summary: each `setItem` starts an independent async chain with no queue or generation check, so last-caller ≠ last-writer.
- failure_scenario: keystroke N's write hits a slow `createWritable()` while keystroke N+1's chain (started 40ms later) completes first; N's `close()` then commits the older payload. The user's last character is silently dropped from persisted state and reappears missing on reload — with no error, since both promises resolve. Note `close()` on OPFS commits the whole swap file, so this is a full-blob clobber, not a partial one. Cheaper: a single-slot "latest value wins" queue (`let inflight; let latest;` — drain to the newest pending value after each write settles), which also collapses N queued keystrokes into one write.

**3. `getRoot()` re-acquires the OPFS root and re-walks the directory tree on every call**
- File: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:49-55`, called at `:89, :109, :128, :142, :159`
- Summary: no memoization of the root handle or of resolved directory handles; every op pays `navigator.storage.getDirectory()` plus one `getDirectoryHandle` round-trip per path segment.
- failure_scenario: `writeFile("state/workspace-zustand-v1.json")` costs 2 extra async hops (getDirectory + getDirectoryHandle("state", {create:true})) before any useful work — repeated per keystroke under finding 1, and multiplied per segment once S4 moves to the `workspaces/<slug>/artifacts/<type>/v0001.md` layout from `paths.ts` (4 segments = 5 hops per file). Cheaper: memoize the root as a module-level `Promise<OpfsDirHandle>` (re-entrant-safe, still lazy so the SSR/unavailable guard still throws on first use) and add a `Map<string, Promise<OpfsDirHandle>>` handle cache keyed by dir path.

**4. `createWritable()`/`close()` per write rewrites the whole blob**
- File: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:112-119`
- Summary: `createWritable()` without `{ keepExistingData: true }` allocates a fresh swap file that `close()` atomically renames — a full copy + fsync-class commit per call.
- failure_scenario: combined with finding 1, every keystroke triggers a full multi-hundred-KB swap-file write and commit on the main thread's task queue, contending with React render work; OPFS `close()` is the expensive part and is not cancellable, so a burst of typing queues unbounded commits. Cheaper: debounce (finding 1) is the primary fix; for the S3 worker proxy, `createSyncAccessHandle()` in a Worker avoids the swap-file round-trip entirely.

**5. `onRehydrateStorage` still probes localStorage directly, bypassing the new seam**
- File: `/repo/app/lib/stores/workspaceStore.ts:533-541`
- Summary: the post-hydration migration check hardcodes `localStorage.getItem("workspace-zustand-v1")` even though `storage` is now pluggable, so under flag ON it always sees "no zustand data".
- failure_scenario: with the corpus flag on and a legacy `workspace-v2` key present, `hasZustandData` is always false → `migrateFromV2()` (`:251`) runs on *every* page load, re-reading and re-parsing the whole v2 blob and calling `setState` — which itself fires another full OPFS write chain — and overwrites the state just hydrated from OPFS. Wasted parse + wasted write + clobbered corpus state on each reload. Cheaper: derive the check from the `_state` argument already passed to the callback (it holds the hydrated state) instead of re-reading and re-parsing storage at all; that also removes the redundant `JSON.parse` on the OFF path.

**6. `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` constructed per call in the manifest codec**
- File: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/manifest.ts:57` and `:78`

- File: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63` (vs `:29-39`)
- Summary: the flag-ON storage seam writes synchronously-per-`set()` while the flag-OFF seam coalesces to one write per 300ms idle.
- failure_scenario: typing 40 chars into the source textarea (~5s) fires ~40 `setItem`s. Cheaper: wrap `createCorpusBackedStorage` in the same debounce (or hoist the debounce above the seam so both adapters inherit it), keeping only the latest value.

**2. No write serialization — concurrent OPFS writes can commit out of order**
- File: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63`
- Summary: each `setItem` starts an independent async chain with no queue or generation check, so last-caller ≠ last-writer.
- failure_scenario: keystroke N's write hits a slow `createWritable()` while keystroke N+1's chain (started 40ms later) completes first; N's `close()` then commits the older payload. Read the full diff and the enclosing sources. Here are the candidates.

## Candidate findings

**1. `app/lib/corpus/flag.ts:16` — optional chaining defeats Next.js `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` build-time inlining, so the documented env flag silently never works in the browser.**

```ts
if (typeof process !== "undefined" && process.env?.NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS === "1") return true;
```
Next.js/webpack `DefinePlugin` substitutes the *exact* member expression `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS`; an `OptionalMemberExpression` (`process.env?.X`) is not matched and is left as a runtime lookup against the client-side `process.env` shim, which contains only inlined keys.
failure_scenario: dev sets `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1` in `.env.local`, runs `next dev`/`next build`. Server-side module eval (where real `process.env` exists) resolves the flag to `true`; the client bundle resolves it to `false`. Since `skipHydration: true` means storage is only exercised client-side, the developer gets plain localStorage while believing OPFS is active — and the header comment at lines 9-10 documents the env path as a supported way to enable it. No test covers the env branch (`workspaceStore-corpus-flag.test.ts` only exercises the localStorage branch).

**2. `app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:117-118` — `finally { await w.close() }` can overwrite the quota error and commits a truncated file.**

```ts
try { await w.write(bytes); } finally { await w.close(); }
```
failure_scenario: OPFS quota is exhausted mid-write. `w.write()` rejects with `QuotaExceededError`; the `finally` block then awaits `w.close()`, which for a stream in an errored/partially-written state rejects (e.g. `InvalidStateError`/`QuotaExceededError` on commit) or resolves after committing the partial bytes. If `close()` rejects, its rejection *replaces* the pending quota rejection, so `wrap()` at line 121 sees a non-quota `DOMException` and produces `{kind:"io"}` instead of `{kind:"quota-exceeded", substrate:"opfs"}` — exactly the G7 contract the file header (lines 12-15) claims to guarantee. If `close()` resolves, the swap file is committed and `state/workspace-zustand-v1.json` is left truncated/corrupt on disk while the caller sees an error. The existing quota test dodges this by throwing from `createWritable()`, never from `write()`. Correct shape is `await w.write(...)` then `await w.close()` on success, with `w.abort()` (or close inside its own try) on failure.

**3. `app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63` — the corpus path drops the 300ms debounce and has no error handling, contradicting the "pure substrate swap" comment (lines 9-11).**

`createDebouncedLocalStorage` coalesces writes and catches quota; `createCorpusBackedStorage.setItem` does neither.
failure_scenario (timing): user types in the source-text textarea with the flag on. Zustand persist fires `setItem` per keystroke; each call starts an independent, unawaited `writeFile` → `createWritable`/`write`/`close` sequence on the *same* OPFS file. OPFS writables are swap-file based and the last `close()` to land wins, so if the promise for keystroke N+1 completes before keystroke N's (entirely possible — separate handle acquisitions with independent `getDirectoryHandle` walks), the older state is committed last and the newest keystrokes are silently lost on the next reload.
failure_scenario (errors): under quota pressure, `writeFile` rejects with a `CorpusError`. Zustand's persist does not attach a rejection handler to a `setItem` promise, so this surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection rather than any UI, i.e. the failure is *less* visible than the `console.warn` on the localStorage path it replaced.

**4. `app/lib/corpus/manifest.ts:87, 94, 103` — `.filter()` silently drops malformed entries, so the "FAIL-LOUD" contract (header lines 12-16) does not hold for the common corruption shapes.**

```ts
? raw.sources.filter(isObject).map((s) => { ... })
...
? raw.customTypeIds.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === "string")
```
failure_scenario: a partially-truncated or half-migrated `workspace.json` contains `"sources": [null, {"id":"s1","ext":"pdf"}, "s2"]` and `"customTypeIds": ["custom-eth", null]`. `filter(isObject)` removes `null` and `"s2"` before `map` ever sees them, and `filter(typeof === "string")` removes the null id. `parseManifest` returns successfully with 1 source and 1 custom type — precisely the "this workspace has no work in it" masquerade the header says must never happen. The `fail("source entry missing id/ext")` guard at line 88 only fires for entries that *are* objects but lack fields, which is the one case the test at `__tests__/manifest.test.ts` happens to cover. Also note `Array.isArray([])`-vs-missing is not distinguished, and `manifestVersion` is accepted as *any* number (line 84) with no check against `MANIFEST_VERSION`, so a future v2 manifest is parsed as if it were v1.

**5. `app/lib/corpus/paths.ts:36-47` (`workspaceSlug`) — sanitization is lossy and non-injective; distinct workspace titles collapse to the same directory.**

Every non-`[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run becomes a single `-`, then `-{2,}` collapses further, then `toLowerCase()`.
failure_scenario: user has workspaces titled `"Study A/B"`, `"Study A-B"`, and `"study a b"`. All three produce `study-a-b`, so `workspaceManifestPath()` returns the identical `workspaces/study-a-b/workspace.json` for all three. Creating the second workspace overwrites the first's manifest and its `artifacts/<type>/v####.md` files land in the same directory, interleaving two workspaces' version histories. There is no collision detection and no reverse mapping stored anywhere. Related: any all-non-ASCII title (`"研究ノート"`, `"Проект"`) throws from line 44 because NFKD does not ASCII-fold CJK/Cyrillic — a non-English user simply cannot create a workspace, and the thrower is a bare `Error`, not a `CorpusError`, so it escapes the typed error model the rest of the layer is built on.

**6. `app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:115-116` — the comment describes a defensive buffer copy that the code does not perform.**

```ts
// Pass a fresh ArrayBuffer view; some implementations dislike shared buffers.
await w.write(bytes);
```
failure_scenario: any caller who passes a *view* into a larger/pooled buffer — e.g. `new Uint8Array(pool, offset, len)` from a future S2/S4 chunked-write or a Node-side `Buffer` (which is a view into an 8KB pool) — relies on the offset/length being honored. If an implementation (or a `Buffer` reaching this path) writes the backing buffer rather than the view, the file gets pool garbage. The comment asserts a mitigation is in place, so a reviewer or later author will not add the `bytes.slice()` that the in-memory fake *does* perform (`inMemoryCorpusFs.ts:23`). Lower confidence than the others — per spec `write(BufferSource)` honors the view — but the fake and the adapter now differ in copy semantics while the contract suite claims to prove substitutability, and no contract case passes an offset view.

## Also noticed (lower confidence, listing for the verify step)

- `app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:602` (`isNotFound`) treats `TypeMismatchError` as not-found. `readdir("a/b/c.txt")` where `c.txt` is a file returns `[]` (looks like "empty directory") rather than an error; likewise `readFile` on a path whose parent segment is a file returns `null` instead of signalling the structural conflict.
- `app/lib/corpus/opfsAdapter.ts:60` — `if (!name)` is a truthiness check on a string; harmless today (`"0"` is truthy) but the guard also misfires for `splitPath("")`, producing `{kind:"io"}` where `readdir`'s contract would want `[]`. `readdir` avoids `splitPath` entirely, so the two path parsers can drift.
- `app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:9-11` header references `layout.ts`, which `CLAUDE.md:52` explicitly says does not exist (it is `paths.ts`, renamed because `layout.ts` is a reserved Next.js filename).

## Verification of the "moved verbatim" claim

The OFF path is genuinely byte-for-byte: `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:25-46` matches the deleted `createDebouncedStorage` in `main:app/lib/stores/workspaceStore.ts` line-for-line (300ms debounce, `clearTimeout` on re-entry, `try/catch` + `console.warn` on quota, `removeItem` cancelling the pending timer and nulling it). Only the function name and the return-type annotation (`StateStorage` instead of the inline object type) changed; no runtime difference. The invariants of the deleted code are preserved **only when the flag is off**. Everything below is about the ON path, where each deleted invariant is dropped without replacement.

## Findings

**1. `/repo/app/lib/stores/workspaceStore.ts:533-539` — v2-migration probe still reads localStorage, so with the corpus flag ON it re-migrates (and clobbers) on every load.**
`onRehydrateStorage` decides "has the zustand store any data?" by `localStorage.getItem("workspace-zustand-v1")`. When the flag is on, the persist blob lives at OPFS `state/workspace-zustand-v1.json`, so this probe is always `null`.
*Failure scenario:* a dev with a legacy `workspace-v2` key enables the flag, works for an hour (state written to OPFS), reloads. Hydration correctly restores the OPFS state, then the post-rehydrate callback sees `zustandRaw === null`, calls `migrateFromV2()`, and `useWorkspaceStore.setState(...)` overwrites `sourceText`/`leanCode`/`decomposition`/`artifacts` with the stale v2 snapshot — which is then written back to OPFS. The hour of work is gone, and this repeats every reload. This also directly contradicts `flag.ts:5-7` ("enabling this starts from an EMPTY corpus and does not carry existing localStorage work over").

**2. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63` — quota/IO errors are no longer swallowed anywhere; they surface as unhandled promise rejections.**
The deleted code wrapped `localStorage.setItem` in `try/catch` + `console.warn`. In zustand 5.0.13 (`node_modules/zustand/esm/middleware.mjs:358-372`), the persist `set` wrapper does `set(...args); return setItem();` — the promise is returned to the action, and store actions like `setSourceText: (v) => set({ sourceText: v })` are called from event handlers that ignore the return value. Nothing ever attaches a `.catch`.
*Failure scenario:* OPFS quota is exhausted mid-session. `wrap()` (`opfsAdapter.ts:79-83`) throws `CorpusError{kind:"quota-exceeded"}`, which rejects the floating `setItem()` promise → an `unhandledrejection` per keystroke (Next.js dev error overlay pops repeatedly; in prod it goes to whatever global handler exists, or nowhere). The user sees no warning, keeps typing, and loses everything on reload — the exact case the deleted `console.warn` existed to make visible.

**3. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63` — the 300ms debounce is gone on the corpus path, so every `set()` issues a full-blob OPFS write with no ordering guarantee.**
The deleted adapter existed specifically to "avoid `JSON.stringify` on every keystroke"; the ON path does `JSON.stringify` of the whole partialized state **plus** a `getFileHandle`/`createWritable`/`write`/`close` round-trip per `set()`.
*Failure scenario:* Lean streaming appends tokens via `setLeanCode` (`app/page.tsx:605`) at chunk rate; each chunk fires an independent, unawaited async write of the entire workspace blob. Two writables on the same file overlap: either the later `createWritable()` rejects with `NoModificationAllowedError` (wrapped as `CorpusError{kind:"io"}` → see finding 2), or writes complete out of order and an earlier, shorter blob lands last, truncating the file to a stale state. Neither is possible on the debounced localStorage path.

**4. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:57-60` with `/repo/app/lib/stores/workspaceStore.ts:501` — `getItem` became async, so `rehydrate()` no longer completes synchronously and can overwrite user input.**
`createJSONStorage` (`middleware.mjs:294-298`) propagates the Promise, and `toThenable` (`:305`) only short-circuits for non-Promise results. content.text: Five of the finders have reported; three are still running (ae9cb819, af96e99e, aef09972). I'll consolidate and launch the verification pass once those last three come back — their completion notifications will re-invoke me. So far the strongest candidates cluster around the corpus-flag ON path: the missing debounce/ordering/error-handling in `storeAdapter.ts`, the localStorage-probing v2 migration in `workspaceStore.ts` that can clobber OPFS state on every reload, the `finally { close() }` quota-error masking in `opfsAdapter.ts`, and the silent-drop `.filter()` validation in `manifest.ts` that contradicts its fail-loud contract.
Six finders in now. Two remain (ae9cb819, af96e99e); their completion notifications will re-invoke me, at which point I'll dedupe the candidate list and launch the adversarial verification pass.

Findings from cross-file tracing (6 candidates, all with concrete failure scenarios):

---

**1. `/repo/app/lib/stores/workspaceStore.ts:533-540` — `onRehydrateStorage` probes localStorage for the store's own blob; with the corpus flag ON it always sees "no data" and re-runs `migrateFromV2()` on every load, clobbering OPFS state.**

The callback still does `localStorage.getItem("workspace-zustand-v1")` to decide `hasZustandData`. Under `resolveWorkspaceStorage()` with the flag on, the blob lives at OPFS `state/workspace-zustand-v1.json`, so that read is `null` forever.

failure_scenario: Dev has legacy `workspace-v2` data in localStorage (very common — that key is written by `saveWorkspace` in `/repo/app/lib/utils/workspacePersistence.ts:109`) and flips `corpus-fs-enabled=1`. On every reload: OPFS hydration merges the real corpus state, then the post-rehydrate callback sees `zustandRaw === null`, calls `migrateFromV2()` (`workspaceStore.ts:251-285`), which `setState`s the stale v2 snapshot over the just-hydrated state. Because zustand's `api.setState` wrapper calls `setItem()` after every set (`zustand/esm/middleware.mjs:365-368`), the stale snapshot is then written back into OPFS — the corpus copy is destroyed, not just shadowed, and the user's work silently reverts to the old localStorage snapshot on each refresh.

---

**2. `/repo/app/page.tsx:78-84` + `/repo/app/page.tsx:321-332` — `persist.rehydrate()` is fire-and-forget, and a later mount effect reads `useWorkspaceStore.getState().decomposition` assuming hydration already finished.**

With `createDebouncedLocalStorage` `getItem` is sync, so `toThenable` resolves inline and the store is populated before the next effect runs. `createCorpusBackedStorage.getItem` (`storeAdapter.ts:57`) is `async`, so hydration finishes a microtask/IO later.

failure_scenario: Flag ON, user has a saved decomposition graph. Mount order: rehydrate() starts (unawaited) → decomp-restore effect runs with `persisted.nodes.length === 0` → `resetDecomp` skipped → the sync-back effect (`page.tsx:338-347`) immediately calls `persistDecompState({nodes: [], ...})`, writing an empty decomposition into the store and hence into OPFS. The graph panel comes up empty and the persisted graph is overwritten with the empty one. Nothing in the codebase reads `persist.hasHydrated()`/`onFinishHydration`, so there is no guard anywhere.

---

**3. `/repo/app/hooks/useWorkspaceSessions.ts:120-140` — session bootstrap/auto-save snapshots the store on mount and keeps full workspace copies in localStorage, forking from the OPFS-backed store.**

`getWorkspaceSnapshot` (`page.tsx:~120`) reads `useWorkspaceStore.getState()` synchronously; the sessions state itself is read/written to `WORKSPACE_SESSIONS_KEY` in localStorage (lines 31, 100, 112).

failure_scenario: Flag ON, first load with existing OPFS content and no sessions yet. The migration effect runs before async hydration completes, `hasWorkspaceContent(ws)` is false (all fields still `DEFAULT_STATE`), so no initial session is created. ```

failure_scenario: Dev follows the module's own docs (and CLAUDE.md), sets `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1` in `.env.local`, rebuilds, and the app silently keeps using localStorage — the shim's `env` has no such key. ---

---

Read the full diff, all 6 new corpus files, the store seam, DD-009, and the S1 plan/checkpoint/test-strategy docs. Five findings; I checked each against the plan's explicit deferrals first.

---

**1. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/flag.ts:15-19` — the "dev-only" guarantee is a comment, not a gate**

The plan's own risk table (`/repo/docs/working/plan-corpus-s1.md:75`) records the mitigation for "enabling the flag silently discards a user's localStorage workspace" as **"Structural: flag is default-off + dev-only (step 7)"**. What shipped is default-off only; `isCorpusEnabled()` reads `localStorage["corpus-fs-enabled"]` with no `process.env.NODE_ENV` check, so the runtime toggle is live in production bundles. The word "dev-only" appears three times in the file header and nowhere in the code.

`failure_scenario`: A user follows a stale dev note / support snippet / their own devtools poking and sets `corpus-fs-enabled=1` in the deployed app. S1 has no migration (plan line 17: flag-ON "initializes clean from `DEFAULT_STATE`"), so on reload they get an empty workspace — sources, artifact version history, and custom types all appear gone. Their localStorage blob is intact, but nothing in the UI says so and there is no path back except knowing to unset a key they can't see. The structural mitigation the plan promised is one `NODE_ENV !== "production"` conjunct; the documented-only version leaves the exact risk the plan claimed to have closed.

---

**2. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:57-66` + `/repo/app/lib/stores/workspaceStore.ts:530` — every reified `CorpusError` is discarded at the only consumer**

`types.ts` builds a substrate-neutral kind union, an exhaustiveness helper, and a worker-serializable twin explicitly to serve DD-009 §Failure-driven ("Silent fallback is disallowed"), and `opfsAdapter.ts` is careful never to `console.warn`-swallow (plan line 76). Then the seam hands those rejections to zustand persist, which has no error path for writes: `middleware.js:365-371` does `api.setState = (...) => { savedSetState(...); return setItem(); }` and every caller discards that promise — a rejected `setItem` is an unhandled rejection, nothing more. On the read side `workspaceStore.ts:530` is `if (error) return;`, which was harmless when `getItem` was synchronous localStorage and now swallows the one channel that carries `unavailable` / `io`. Nothing in the plan or checkpoint defers an error sink; the plan only defers the *UI element*.

`failure_scenario`: OPFS quota fills (or the browser lacks `navigator.storage`, e.g. some private-mode contexts). `getItem` rejects `{kind:"unavailable"}` → `if (error) return` → app renders `DEFAULT_STATE` as if the workspace were new. The user starts typing over it; each `setItem` rejects into the void. They work a full session, close the tab, and lose all of it, having received exactly zero signals — the precise silent-degradation failure the whole error model was built to make impossible, just relocated one layer above the adapter. A single `.catch` at the seam that logs the typed `detail` (a ~5-line sink, not a UI) is the S1-altitude version.

---

**3. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:55` — `state/<name>.json` is hand-concatenated and outside the sanctioned layout**

`paths.ts:15-18` states the invariant explicitly: *"The only source of corpus paths is this module — callers must never hand-concatenate."* The first and only consumer of `CorpusFS` in the codebase violates it on line 55. And the path it invents is not in DD-009's folder layout (`/repo/docs/decisions/009-artifact-corpus-architecture.md:43-68`), which has exactly two top-level entries, `workspaces/` and `settings.json`. I grepped DD-009, the plan, the decomposition, and the checkpoint: `state/` is sanctioned nowhere; the only justification is the code comment on line 50.

`failure_scenario`: S2's FSA mirror copies the OPFS tree into the user's real folder and S3 commits it. An undocumented `state/workspace-zustand-v1.json` — a dev-only blob containing a whole duplicate workspace — lands in the user's git repo and cross-device sync, and the S4 migration (which walks `workspaces/`) never sees it, so any dev work done under the flag is orphaned at exactly the moment migration was supposed to rescue it. The cheap version is `STATE_BLOB_PATH` exported from `paths.ts` and a line in the DD-009 layout block noting it as S1-transitional.

---

**4. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts:61-63` — the corpus branch drops the 300ms debounce with nothing replacing it**

The debounce lives *inside* `createDebouncedLocalStorage`, so it's a property of the OFF adapter rather than of the seam. The ON path issues one full-state serialize + OPFS `createWritable` per zustand `set()` — i.e. per keystroke into `sourceText` — and the calls are unawaited and unserialized.

`failure_scenario`: Fast typing produces overlapping `writeFile` calls on the same OPFS file. Chrome holds an exclusive lock while a writable is open, so the second `createWritable()` rejects with `NoModificationAllowedError`, which `wrap()` maps to `{kind:"io"}` and finding 2 then discards — an intermittent, load-dependent dropped write with no symptom until reload shows stale state. Since the debounce is a property of the seam, not of localStorage, the right depth is a shared decorator (`debounced(storage)`) applied to whichever adapter `resolveWorkspaceStorage` picks.

---

**5. `/repo/app/lib/corpus/paths.ts:36-45` — `workspaceSlug` has no uniquifier and keys directories on a mutable title**

`SAFE_SEGMENT` collapses every unsafe run to a single hyphen, so `"My Paper (v2)"`, `"My Paper v2"`, and `"my—paper—v2"` all produce `my-paper-v2`. I grepped DD-009, `plan-corpus-s1.md`, `decomposition-corpus-architecture.md`, `checkpoint-corpus-s1.md`, and `test-strategy-corpus-s1.md` for collision/uniquifier/duplicate-title: every hit is about *traversal* safety (G10, plan line 77), none about collisions. This is unaddressed, not deferred — and it's an S0 contract that S2/S3/S4 all bind to, which becomes on-disk data in users' git repos.

`failure_scenario`: In S4 a researcher with two similarly-titled workspaces has the second silently resolve onto the first's directory — `workspace.json`, `sources/`, and `artifacts/<type>/v0001.md` interleave, and because artifact versions are content files, git records the clobber as ordinary edits rather than a conflict, defeating the F6 no-loss-provenance property DD-009 exists to guarantee. The related edge: slugging a *mutable* title means renaming a workspace relocates its whole tree, so `git log`/`blame` continuity (DD-009 line 102) breaks on rename. Both dissolve if the directory is keyed on a stable workspace id with the slug as a human-readable prefix — a change that is nearly free now and expensive once corpora exist on users' disks.

All eight finders have now reported. The candidates converge heavily on a few clusters. Consolidating and deduping, I have these candidate findings to verify:

1. `flag.ts:16` env-flag inlining — **conflicting evidence**: my earlier direct check suggested DefinePlugin does inline the optional-chained read, but the cross-file tracer found the un-inlined expression surviving in a checked-in `.next` chunk. Needs a decisive build-based check.
2. `storeAdapter.ts` corpus `setItem`: unserialized overlapping OPFS writes (out-of-order commit → lost state), dropped 300ms debounce, unhandled rejections.
3. `workspaceStore.ts:533-541` — `onRehydrateStorage` probes localStorage directly, so with flag ON it re-runs `migrateFromV2()` every load and clobbers OPFS state.
4. `opfsAdapter.ts:117-118` — `finally { await w.close() }` masks quota errors and commits truncated files.
5. `manifest.ts` — silent-default validation contradicting its own FAIL-LOUD contract.
6. `paths.ts` — slug collisions and bare-Error throw on non-Latin titles.
7. `page.tsx` / `useWorkspaceSessions` — async-hydration races (empty decomposition overwrite, session bootstrap).
8. Flag "dev-only" not enforced; hand-built `state/` path bypassing `paths.ts`; stale `layout.ts` references; plus the reuse/dead-code cluster.

Launching the adversarial verification pass now — eight verifiers, each instructed to refute:

input.prompt:
You are adversarially verifying a code-review finding in /repo (Next.js app, branch `review`). Your job is to decisively CONFIRM or REFUTE it with empirical evidence, not plausibility.

CLAIM: In /repo/app/lib/corpus/flag.ts line ~16, the expression `process.env?.NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS === "1"` uses optional chaining, which allegedly defeats Next.js build-time inlining of NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars, so setting NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS=1 never enables the flag in the client bundle. Supporting evidence offered: a checked-in chunk /repo/.next/static/chunks/07eu2bpgp5ahh.js contains `S.default.env?.NEXT_PUBLIC_CORPUS_FS==="1"` un-inlined. CONFLICTING evidence: a separate check concluded webpack's DefinePlugin DOES inline the optional-chained member expression (webpack 5 parser supports optional chaining in defines).

Resolve this empirically:
1. Read /repo/app/lib/corpus/flag.ts in full.

## Failure modes considered

**Gate decisions (both Round-1 triggers evaluated independently):**
- **`/pre-mortem`: not triggered.** S1 does not meet the high-stakes criteria — it is flag-gated (default-off), fully reversible (new module + one small wiring edit), the slice is ~1100 lines but ~70% tests and no single concern >500 LOC, it crosses no security/auth boundary (OPFS is origin-sandboxed; no untrusted input crosses), and `CorpusFS` is an internal contract, not a public/external API. A pre-mortem already exists at the **DD-009 level** — the Node spike's `/pre-mortem` produced 5 failure narratives (docs/spikes/isomorphic-git-perf-50mb.md §Failure narratives), carried into the decomposition; S1-specific failures are the table below.
- **`/architecture-review`: triggered** — the plan's Files to touch span ≥2 modules (new `app/lib/corpus/` module + `app/lib/stores/` wiring + build/config) and S1 establishes the foundational `CorpusFS` boundary and its dependency direction, which is exactly the structural decision arch-review exists to catch before code commits. Run on this plan; output at `docs/reviews/architecture-review.md`. **Findings 1–3 (substrate-neutral single error-kind source; git as a separate `CorpusGit` interface; DI seam typed as `CorpusFS`) have been folded into steps 1 and 7 above; finding 4 (S4 access-pattern contract case) into the Test specification; finding 5 (no misleading "saved" in S1) noted — confirm during step 7.**

| Failure mode | Guard |
|---|---|
| OPFS adapter "passes" in CI only because jsdom silently lacks OPFS, masking real breakage | Structural: contract suite runs against the in-memory fake in CI AND a Playwright real-OPFS smoke (step 9) gates pre-merge; the SSR-guard test (G8) asserts the no-`navigator.storage` path rejects loudly rather than no-oping |
| Enabling the flag silently discards a user's localStorage workspace (no migration yet) | Structural: flag is default-off + dev-only (step 7); plan + CLAUDE.md state explicitly that S1 flag-ON starts clean and migration is S4; characterization baseline (step 4) proves the OFF path is untouched |
| Quota-exceeded write is swallowed (repeating the existing `console.warn` silent-degradation at workspaceStore.ts:44-46) | Test G7 asserts the adapter rejects with `kind:"opfs-quota-exceeded"`; no `catch`-and-warn in the adapter |
| Workspace title with `..`/`/` escapes the corpus root (path traversal) | Test G10 asserts slug sanitization; layout builders are the only path source |
| Malformed `workspace.json` silently parsed as empty → looks like data loss | Test G12: parse of malformed/empty manifest yields a typed recoverable error, never a default-empty manifest |

## Risks

- **The in-memory fake may diverge from real OPFS semantics** (ordering, async timing, quota behavior). Mitigated not eliminated by the Playwright smoke (step 9) and by keeping the fake minimal/faithful. This is the main residual risk after the plan (test-strategy Summary).
- **Safari/WebKit OPFS is still unmeasured** (both spikes deferred it); S1's Playwright smoke covers Chrome+FF only. Safari stays a pre-launch verification item per the browser smoke spike, not an S1 blocker.
- **Deferred coverage (from test-strategy "Beyond scope"):** multi-tab OPFS contention (matters in S4), and characterization baselines for the other three localStorage stores (`workspace-sessions-v1`, `metaformalism-sessions`, `evidence-store-v1`) — relevant to S4 migration, not S1.
- **Store-wiring creep:** step 7 edits `workspaceStore.ts` (575 lines); if the injectable-adapter change is larger than ~30 lines, extract to `app/lib/corpus/storeAdapter.ts` to stay under the 500-line guideline.

## Rollback

This slice ships no user-visible change (flag default-off), so post-ship rollback is low-stakes:

1. `git revert <s1-merge-sha>` on `main` — removes the entire `app/lib/corpus/` module and the step-7 wiring atomically. Because the flag is default-off, no production data path used the adapter, so revert has no data-state consequence.
2. If only the wiring is suspect (adapter module is harmless dead code), instead revert just the step-7 commit (`git revert <step7-sha>`) to restore the unconditional localStorage adapter selection in `workspaceStore.ts`, leaving the module in place.
3. No schema/data migration to undo (S1 introduces none), no cache to invalidate, no remote/service to restart. No feature flag to flip in prod because it is never enabled in prod.
4. **No irreversible component.** The only persistent side effect possible is OPFS files written during *dev* testing with the flag on; clear them with `await (await navigator.storage.getDirectory()).removeEntry('workspaces', {recursive:true})` in the dev console, or via the browser's site-data clear.
